records.source: Καὶ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον διεπέρασεν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν.
records.gloss: And having got into a boat he crossed over and came into the own town.
pieces: So Jesus got back into the boat, crossed the lake, and came to the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lived.

L.1: And getting into a boat, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} crossed over and came to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own town.

R.1: Jesus got into a boat and went back across the lake to the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lived.

decisions.choice: his own town: Capernaum
decisions.reason: Jesus had moved to Capernaum (4:13).

decisions.choice: Jesus; the lake
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus and say what he crossed.

records.heading: Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man

records.source: Καὶ ἰδοὺ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παραλυτικὸν ἐπὶ κλίνης βεβλημένον.
records.gloss: And behold, they were bringing to him a paralytic on a bed lying.
pieces: Some people brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a paralyzed man lying on a stretcher.

L.2: And look, they were bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a paralyzed man lying on a bed.

R.2: Some people brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a man who could not walk. He was lying on a mat.

decisions.choice: bed: a light pallet or stretcher on which he was carried
decisions.reason: The word means a bed or couch; one that could be carried is meant, as the man picks it up in 9:6.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Θάρσει, τέκνον· ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
records.gloss: And having seen the Jesus the faith of them he said to the paralytic, Take courage, child; are forgiven of you the sins.
pieces: Jesus saw their faith and said to the man, "Be encouraged, my son. Your sins are forgiven."

L.2: And seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralyzed man, "Take heart, child; your sins are forgiven."

R.2: Jesus saw that they had faith in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said to the man, "Cheer up, my friend! Your sins are forgiven."

decisions.choice: their faith: the trust of those who brought him, and his own
decisions.reason: "Their" includes the carriers. Their bringing him showed their trust in Jesus.

decisions.choice: are forgiven: God forgives them now, and Jesus declares it
decisions.reason: The present passive speaks of forgiveness given now; the passive points to God. That Jesus speaks it is what offends the scribes (9:3).

decisions.choice: child: an affectionate address
alternatives: a statement of the man's age
decisions.reason: The word means child, used warmly, as an older person might speak to a younger one.

decisions.choice: Be encouraged, my son (B); Cheer up, my friend (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use natural English for a kind address.

records.source: καὶ ἰδού τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτος βλασφημεῖ.
records.gloss: And behold, some of the scribes said among themselves, This one blasphemes.
pieces: At this some of the scribes said to themselves, "This man is insulting God!"

L.3: And look, some of the scribes said to themselves, "This [man] blasphemes."

R.3: Some of the teachers of the law thought, "This man is speaking as if he were God!"

decisions.choice: blasphemes: insults God by claiming what belongs to God alone
decisions.reason: Only God can forgive sins against him (Isaiah 43:25). To the scribes, Jesus's words claimed God's right.

decisions.choice: is insulting God (B); is speaking as if he were God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the charge means.

decisions.choice: look (L); at this (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: καὶ εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἱνατί ἐνθυμεῖσθε πονηρὰ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: And having known the Jesus the thoughts of them said, Why do you think evil in the hearts of you?
pieces: Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, "Why do you think such evil things in your hearts?

L.4: And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, "Why do you think evil in your hearts?

R.4: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Why are you thinking such evil things?

decisions.choice: knowing their thoughts: Jesus knows what they say only inwardly
decisions.reason: They spoke "to themselves" (9:3). Knowing hearts belongs to God (1 Samuel 16:7; Psalm 139:2).

decisions.choice: evil: wrong and hostile thoughts
decisions.reason: Accusing God's agent of blasphemy is itself wrong in God's sight.

records.source: τί γάρ ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
records.gloss: Which for is easier, to say, Are forgiven of you the sins, or to say, Get up and walk?
pieces: Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?

L.5: For which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?

R.5: Is it easier to say to this man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?

decisions.choice: which is easier to say: forgiveness cannot be seen, healing can
decisions.reason: Anyone can say "your sins are forgiven" with no one able to check. A command to walk is tested at once. The healing will show that the unseen word was true.

records.source: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας τότε λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Ἐγερθεὶς ἆρόν σου τὴν κλίνην καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
records.gloss: So that but you may know that authority has the Son of the Man on the earth to forgive sins, then he says to the paralytic, Having got up take up of you the bed and go to the house of you.
pieces: But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "Get up, pick up your stretcher, and go home."

L.6: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the paralyzed man—"Get up, take up your bed and go to your home."

R.6: I will show you that the Son of Man has the right to forgive sins here on earth." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man who could not walk, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home."

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: Jesus turns from the scribes to the man
decisions.reason: Jesus begins a sentence to the scribes and finishes it with action: the command to the paralyzed man.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man has authority on earth: the figure of Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: any human being has such authority
decisions.reason: In Daniel the one like a son of man receives authority from God. Jesus claims that authority now, on earth, to forgive sins (see 8:20).

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense.

records.source: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having got up he went away to the house of him.
pieces: And the man got up and went home.

L.7: And he got up and went away to his home.

R.7: And the man got up and went home.

decisions.choice: he got up and went: he does just what he was told
decisions.reason: The words repeat the command of 9:6. The healing is complete and immediate.

records.source: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐφοβήθησαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν τὸν δόντα ἐξουσίαν τοιαύτην τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
records.gloss: Having seen then the crowds were afraid and glorified the God the having given authority such to the men.
pieces: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe, and they glorified God for giving such authority to human beings.

L.8: And when the crowds saw [it], they were afraid, and they glorified God, who had given such authority to {{gender:human beings|men}}.

R.8: When the people saw this, they were amazed and afraid. They gave glory to God for giving such power to people.

decisions.choice: were afraid: were filled with awe at God's power
decisions.reason: Fear here is the awe people feel before God's work.

decisions.choice: to human beings: to Jesus as a man, and perhaps to those who will act in his name
decisions.reason: The crowds see a man forgive sins. The plural may also look ahead to the authority Jesus gives his followers (16:19; 18:18).

decisions.choice: were afraid, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: marveled, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "marveled". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.source: Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, Μαθθαῖον λεγόμενον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And passing on the Jesus from there saw a man sitting at the tax booth, Matthew called, and he says to him, Follow me; and having got up he followed him.
pieces: Moving on from there, Jesus noticed a man called Matthew at his seat in the tax office. Jesus said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." And Matthew rose and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.9: And as Jesus passed on from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." And he got up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.9: As Jesus walked on from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a man named Matthew. Matthew was sitting at the place where he collected taxes. Jesus said to him, "Come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." So Matthew got up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the tax booth: where tolls were collected on goods passing through
alternatives: a government office for income tax
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on a trade route and near the border of Herod Antipas's territory. Toll collectors were despised (5:46).

decisions.choice: Matthew: the tax collector whom Mark and Luke call Levi
decisions.reason: Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27 tell the same call of "Levi". Matthew 10:3 calls him "Matthew the tax collector". Early Christian tradition named this Matthew as the author of the Gospel; the Gospel itself does not say who wrote it.

decisions.choice: he got up and followed him: an immediate response, leaving his work
decisions.reason: As with the fishermen (4:20, 22), Matthew leaves his trade at once.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense.

records.heading: The call of Matthew

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And it happened of him reclining in the house, and behold, many tax collectors and sinners having come were reclining with the Jesus and the disciples of him.
pieces: Then, as Jesus sat at table in the house, a crowd of tax collectors and sinners came and joined {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples for the meal.

L.10: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table] in the house, look, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

R.10: Later Jesus was eating a meal in the house. Many tax collectors and other people known as sinners came and ate with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers.

decisions.choice: the house: probably Matthew's
decisions.reason: Luke 5:29 says Levi gave a feast in his house. Matthew says only "the house".

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for living outside God's law
decisions.reason: The word marked people whose way of life put them outside respectable religious society, such as those in shameful trades.

decisions.choice: reclining with: sharing a meal, a sign of acceptance
alternatives: only being in the same room
decisions.reason: Eating with someone showed fellowship. That is why the Pharisees object (9:11).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: And having seen the Pharisees were saying to the disciples of him, Why with the tax collectors and sinners eats the teacher of you?
pieces: When the Pharisees saw it, they asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"

L.11: And when the Pharisees saw [this], they said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"

R.11: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: careful about purity at meals
alternatives: opposed to all meals with others
decisions.reason: The Pharisees kept rules of purity at their tables. Eating with people who did not keep the law would make a teacher unclean in their eyes.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας εἶπεν· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες.
records.gloss: He but having heard said, Not need have the being strong of a physician but the badly having.
pieces: Jesus heard them and said, "People who are well do not need a doctor; sick people do.

L.12: But hearing [this], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.

R.12: Jesus heard this. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Healthy people do not need a doctor. Sick people do.

decisions.choice: the physician and the sick: Jesus came for those who know they need him
decisions.reason: The proverb pictures Jesus as a doctor and sinners as the sick. It does not say the Pharisees are well; it says why he is with sinners.

records.source: πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν· οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς.
records.gloss: Having gone but learn what is: Mercy I want and not sacrifice; not for I came to call righteous but sinners.
pieces: Go and learn what this saying means: 'I want mercy, not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners."

L.13: But go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call [the] righteous, but sinners."

R.13: Go and find out what this Scripture means: 'I want you to show mercy to people, more than I want you to offer sacrifices.' I did not come to invite good people. I came to invite sinners."

decisions.choice: I desire mercy, not sacrifice: Hosea 6:6
decisions.reason: In Hosea God says he wants faithful love more than offerings. The "not" ranks the two, as Hebrew often does. Jesus quotes it again in 12:7.

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who think they are right with God
alternatives: people who truly have no sin
decisions.reason: There is irony: those who count themselves righteous do not see their need.

decisions.choice: to call: to invite, as to a feast and into the kingdom
decisions.reason: The verb is used of inviting guests (22:3-9).

decisions.choice: more than I want you to offer sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the saying ranks mercy above sacrifice.

records.source: Τότε προσέρχονται αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου λέγοντες· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύομεν πολλά, οἱ δὲ μαθηταί σου οὐ νηστεύουσιν;
records.gloss: Then come to him the disciples of John saying, Why we and the Pharisees fast often, the but disciples of you not fast?
pieces: Next John's disciples came and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We fast often, and so do the Pharisees. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not fast?"

L.14: Then the disciples of John come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples do not fast?"

R.14: Then the followers of John the Baptist came to Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We and the Pharisees often go without food to pray. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers not do that?"

decisions.choice: we and the Pharisees fast: regular fasting as a mark of devotion
alternatives: the fast of the Day of Atonement only
decisions.reason: Besides the fast the law required, devout groups fasted regularly (6:16; Luke 18:12).

decisions.choice: often, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the word is missing in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "often". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: come (L); came (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense.

records.heading: A question about fasting

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος πενθεῖν ἐφ’ ὅσον μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ὁ νυμφίος;
records.gloss: And said to them the Jesus, Not can the sons of the bridal chamber mourn as long as with them is the bridegroom?
pieces: Jesus answered, "How can the wedding guests mourn while the bridegroom is with them?

L.15: And Jesus said to them, "Can the {{gender:guests|sons}} of the bridal chamber mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them?

R.15: Jesus said to them, "Friends of a bridegroom do not feel sad while he is with them at the wedding.

decisions.choice: sons of the bridal chamber: the groom's friends and guests at a wedding
decisions.reason: "Sons of" describes those who belong to something. A wedding was a time of feasting, when no one fasted.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: Jesus, as God is the bridegroom of his people
decisions.reason: In the prophets God is Israel's husband (Isaiah 62:5; Hosea 2:19). Jesus takes that picture for himself, and John's disciples would know the Baptist's words in John 3:29.

decisions.choice: the wedding guests (B); friends of a bridegroom (R)
alternatives: the sons of the bridal chamber
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant. The bridegroom is a figure in a picture, so his pronoun takes no deity_pronoun span, as in John 3:29.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects "no"; Readable gives the answer.

records.source: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν.
records.gloss: Will come but days when will be taken away from them the bridegroom, and then they will fast.
pieces: But a time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them, and then they will fast.

L.15: But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.

R.15: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will go without food.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom taken away: a hint of Jesus's death
decisions.reason: "Taken away" suggests a violent removal. This is the first hint in Matthew of Jesus's death.

records.source: οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐπιβάλλει ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ παλαιῷ· αἴρει γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱματίου, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.
records.gloss: No one but puts a patch of cloth unshrunk on a garment old; takes away for the fullness of it from the garment, and worse tear happens.
pieces: No one sews a patch of new, unshrunk cloth onto an old coat. The patch will pull away from the coat, and the tear will be worse.

L.16: And no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear results.

R.16: No one uses a piece of new cloth to fix a hole in old clothes. The new cloth will shrink and pull away, and the hole will get bigger.

decisions.choice: the new patch and the old garment: what Jesus brings cannot be added to the old ways as a repair
decisions.reason: With the wineskins (9:17), the picture answers the question about fasting. The new time Jesus brings needs new forms.

records.source: οὐδὲ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, ῥήγνυνται οἱ ἀσκοί, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπόλλυνται· ἀλλὰ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς, καὶ ἀμφότεροι συντηροῦνται.
records.gloss: Nor do they put wine new into wineskins old; if but not, burst the wineskins, and the wine is poured out and the wineskins are destroyed; but they put wine new into wineskins fresh, and both are preserved.
pieces: And people do not pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will split, the wine will run out, and the skins will be ruined. No, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are kept safe."

L.17: Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, and the wine is poured out and the wineskins are destroyed. But they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved."

R.17: People do not put new wine into old leather bags. If they do, the bags will break, the wine will spill, and the bags will be ruined. People always put new wine into new bags. Then both the wine and the bags are kept safe."

decisions.choice: wineskins: bags made of goatskin
decisions.reason: New wine was still fermenting and stretched the skin. An old skin, already stretched and dry, would split.

decisions.choice: both are preserved: the new is kept, and nothing is wasted
alternatives: the old is kept as well
decisions.reason: Matthew alone adds these words. They stress that what is new must be given a fitting form so it is not lost.

decisions.choice: leather bags
decisions.reason: Readable describes them.

records.source: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτοῖς ἰδοὺ ἄρχων εἷς ἐλθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ μου ἄρτι ἐτελεύτησεν· ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν ἐπίθες τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπ’ αὐτήν, καὶ ζήσεται.
records.gloss: These things of him speaking to them behold, a ruler one having come was kneeling to him saying, The daughter of me just died; but having come lay the hand of you on her, and she will live.
pieces: While Jesus was still speaking, a leader came and knelt in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "My daughter has just died," he said. "But come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand on her, and she will live."

L.18: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying these things to them, look, a ruler came and knelt before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "My daughter has just died, but come and lay {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand on her, and she will live."

R.18: While Jesus was saying these things, a leader came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He bowed down in front of Jesus and said, "My daughter has just died. But come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand on her, and she will live again."

decisions.choice: a ruler: a leader of the synagogue
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "a ruler". Mark 5:22 and Luke 8:41 name him Jairus, a leader of the synagogue.

decisions.choice: has just died
decisions.reason: Matthew tells the story briefly, and the father's faith asks for life from the dead.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: A leader's daughter and a woman's faith

records.source: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having got up the Jesus followed him and the disciples of him.
pieces: Jesus got up and went with him, and so did {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

L.19: And Jesus got up and followed him, and [so did] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

R.19: So Jesus got up and went with him. His followers went too.

decisions.choice: followed him: went with him
decisions.reason: Here the verb simply means going along with someone.

records.source: Καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ αἱμορροοῦσα δώδεκα ἔτη προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: And behold, a woman suffering bleeding twelve years having come behind touched the fringe of the garment of him;
pieces: Then a woman came up behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. For twelve years she had suffered from bleeding. She touched the tassel on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak.

L.20: And look, a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years came up behind [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and touched the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment,

R.20: Then a woman came up behind Jesus. She had been bleeding for twelve years. She touched the edge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes.

decisions.choice: bleeding: a flow of blood that made her ritually unclean
decisions.reason: A woman with such bleeding was unclean, and so was anything she touched (Leviticus 15:25-27). For twelve years she had been cut off from worship.

decisions.choice: the fringe: the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak
decisions.reason: The law told Israelites to wear tassels to remind them of God's commands (Numbers 15:38-39). Jesus wore them.

decisions.choice: look (L); then (B, R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ἐν ἑαυτῇ· Ἐὰν μόνον ἅψωμαι τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.
records.gloss: was saying for in herself, If only I touch the garment of him I will be saved.
pieces: She thought, "If I can just touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak, I will be made well."

L.21: for she was saying to herself, "If I only touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment, I will be saved."

R.21: She said to herself, "If I can just touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes, I will be healed."

decisions.choice: saved: made well, and more than that, rescued
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:21 ("he will save his people"). Here it means healing, but Matthew's readers hear the wider sense of being rescued by Jesus.

decisions.choice: saved (L); made well (B); healed (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word's wider sense; Balanced and Readable say what she hoped for, and the meaning note explains the rest.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς στραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Θάρσει, θύγατερ· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
records.gloss: The but Jesus having turned and having seen her said, Take courage, daughter; the faith of you has saved you.
pieces: Jesus turned around, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw her, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Courage, my daughter! Your faith has made you well."

L.22: But Jesus turned, and seeing her, said, "Take heart, daughter; your faith has saved you."

R.22: Jesus turned and saw her. He said, "Cheer up, my daughter! You are healed because of your faith."

decisions.choice: saved: made well, and more than that, rescued
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:21 ("he will save his people"). Here it means healing, but Matthew's readers hear the wider sense of being rescued by Jesus.

decisions.choice: daughter: a warm address that takes her into God's family
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to an outcast woman as a member of the family.

decisions.choice: saved (L); made well (B); healed (R)
decisions.reason: As in 9:21.

records.source: καὶ ἐσώθη ἡ γυνὴ ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
records.gloss: And was saved the woman from the hour that.
pieces: And from that moment the woman was well.

L.22: And the woman was saved from that hour.

R.22: The woman was healed from that moment.

decisions.choice: saved: made well, and more than that, rescued
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:21 ("he will save his people"). Here it means healing, but Matthew's readers hear the wider sense of being rescued by Jesus.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς αὐλητὰς καὶ τὸν ὄχλον θορυβούμενον ἔλεγεν· Ἀναχωρεῖτε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν τὸ κοράσιον ἀλλὰ καθεύδει· καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having come the Jesus into the house of the ruler and having seen the flute players and the crowd making a commotion \v 24 he was saying, Go away, not for died the girl but sleeps; and they were laughing at him.
pieces: When Jesus came to the leader's house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.
"Go away," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "The girl is not dead; she is asleep." But they laughed at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.23: And when Jesus came into the ruler's house and saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion,
L.24: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Go away, for the girl is not dead but sleeping." And they laughed at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.23: Jesus came to the leader's house. He saw people playing flutes for a funeral and a crowd making a lot of noise.
R.24: He said, "Go away. The girl is not dead. She is only sleeping." But the people laughed at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: flute players: hired mourners for a funeral
decisions.reason: Funerals had flute players and wailing mourners. Later Jewish teaching said even the poorest man should hire at least two flutes for his wife's funeral (Mishnah, Ketubot 4:4).

decisions.choice: sleeping: she is dead, but for God it is like sleep, from which he will wake her
decisions.reason: The crowd knows she is dead, which is why they laugh. Jesus speaks of death as sleep, as Scripture sometimes does (Daniel 12:2; John 11:11-14).

records.source: ὅτε δὲ ἐξεβλήθη ὁ ὄχλος, εἰσελθὼν ἐκράτησεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἠγέρθη τὸ κοράσιον.
records.gloss: When but was put out the crowd, having gone in he took hold of the hand of her, and was raised the girl.
pieces: After the crowd had been sent outside, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.

L.25: But when the crowd had been put out, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went in and took her by the hand, and the girl got up.

R.25: After the people were sent outside, Jesus went in and took the girl's hand, and she got up.

decisions.choice: got up: was raised, the word used of rising from the dead
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Jesus's resurrection (16:21; 28:6).

decisions.choice: took her by the hand: touching a dead body
decisions.reason: Touching a corpse made a person unclean (Numbers 19:11). As with the leper (8:3), Jesus's touch brings life instead.

records.source: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ φήμη αὕτη εἰς ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἐκείνην.
records.gloss: And went out the report this into all the land that.
pieces: News of this spread through the whole region.

L.26: And this report went out into all that land.

R.26: The news about this spread all over that area.

decisions.choice: the news spread: Jesus's fame grows
decisions.reason: Matthew records the spread of the news without saying who told it.

records.source: Καὶ παράγοντι ἐκεῖθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ δύο τυφλοὶ κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες· Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὲ Δαυίδ.
records.gloss: And passing on from there the Jesus followed him two blind crying out and saying, Have mercy on us, son of David.
pieces: Two blind men followed Jesus as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place. They kept shouting, "Son of David, have mercy on us!"

L.27: And as Jesus passed on from there, two blind [men] followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, crying out and saying, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"

R.27: As Jesus left there, two blind men followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They shouted, "Son of David, please have pity on us!"

decisions.choice: Son of David: a title for the promised king
decisions.reason: The title names Jesus as the Messiah (1:1). The prophets said the blind would see when God came to save (Isaiah 35:5).

decisions.choice: two blind men
decisions.reason: As with the two men in 8:28, Matthew tells of two.

records.heading: Two blind men

records.source: ἐλθόντι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ τυφλοί, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι;
records.gloss: Having come then into the house came to him the blind, and says to them the Jesus, Do you believe that I am able this to do?
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had gone indoors, the blind men came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and Jesus asked them, "Do you believe that I can do this?"

L.28: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come into the house, the blind [men] came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and Jesus says to them, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?"

R.28: When Jesus went into the house, the blind men came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Jesus asked them, "Do you believe that I can make you see?"

decisions.choice: believe: trust that Jesus can do it
decisions.reason: Jesus asks for trust in his power, as with the centurion (8:10).

decisions.choice: make you see
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this" is.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε.
records.gloss: They say to him, Yes, Lord.
pieces: "Yes, Lord," they said.

decisions.choice: Lord: the address of faith
decisions.reason: As in 8:2, 6 and 25.

records.source: τότε ἥψατο τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν λέγων· Κατὰ τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν γενηθήτω ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Then he touched the eyes of them saying, According to the faith of you let it be to you.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched their eyes and said, "Because of your faith, let it be done for you."

L.29: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched their eyes, saying, "According to your faith let it be done to you."

R.29: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched their eyes and said, "You have faith, so it will happen for you."

decisions.choice: according to your faith: as you have trusted
alternatives: in proportion to how much faith you have
decisions.reason: As with the centurion (8:13), the healing answers their trust.

records.source: καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί.
records.gloss: And were opened of them the eyes.
pieces: And their sight was restored.

decisions.choice: their eyes were opened: they could see
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual one for giving sight to the blind (20:33).

records.source: καὶ ἐνεβριμήθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε μηδεὶς γινωσκέτω·
records.gloss: And sternly warned them the Jesus saying, See no one let know;
pieces: Jesus warned them sternly, "Make sure that no one hears about this."

L.30: And Jesus sternly warned them, saying, "See that no one knows [about this]."

R.30: Jesus gave them a strong warning: "Do not let anyone know about this."

decisions.choice: sternly warned: spoke to them with great force
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong one, used of snorting with anger or of a stern order.

decisions.choice: let no one know: as with the leper (8:4)
decisions.reason: Jesus does not want fame as a wonder-worker to shape what people expect of the Son of David. The reason is not stated.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες διεφήμισαν αὐτὸν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ.
records.gloss: They but having gone out spread abroad him in all the land that.
pieces: But they went out and spread the word about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all over that region.

L.31: But they went out and spread the news about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in all that land.

R.31: But the two men went out and told everyone in that whole area about Jesus.

decisions.choice: but they spread the news: they disobey at once
decisions.reason: Matthew tells the disobedience plainly, without comment.

records.source: Αὐτῶν δὲ ἐξερχομένων ἰδοὺ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπον κωφὸν δαιμονιζόμενον·
records.gloss: Of them then going out behold, they brought to him a man mute demon-possessed;
pieces: As they were leaving, some people brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a man who could not speak because he was controlled by a demon.

L.32: And as they were going out, look, they brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a man who was mute and demon-possessed.

R.32: As the two men were leaving, some people brought another man to Jesus. This man could not talk because he had a demon in him.

decisions.choice: mute: unable to speak, perhaps also deaf
decisions.reason: The word can mean deaf or mute; 9:33 shows that speech is the point.

decisions.choice: mute and demon-possessed: the demon caused the silence
decisions.reason: When the demon leaves, the man speaks (9:33).

decisions.choice: because he was controlled by a demon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the link that 9:33 shows.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.heading: A man who could not speak

records.source: καὶ ἐκβληθέντος τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός.
records.gloss: And having been cast out the demon spoke the mute.
pieces: When the demon was driven out, the man who had been mute began to speak.

L.33: And when the demon had been cast out, the mute [man] spoke.

R.33: Jesus made the demon leave, and the man began to talk.

decisions.choice: having been cast out: by Jesus
decisions.reason: The passive does not name Jesus, but he is plainly the one who acts.

decisions.choice: Jesus made the demon leave
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες· Οὐδέποτε ἐφάνη οὕτως ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: And marveled the crowds saying, Never appeared thus in the Israel.
pieces: The crowds were astonished. "Israel has never seen anything like this!" they said.

L.33: And the crowds marveled, saying, "Never has anything like this appeared in Israel."

R.33: The people were amazed. They said, "We have never seen anything like this in Israel!"

decisions.choice: never in Israel: the works of chapters 8-9 are something new
decisions.reason: The crowds' words sum up the healings since 8:1.

records.source: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον· Ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
records.gloss: The but Pharisees were saying, By the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons.
pieces: But the Pharisees kept saying, "It is by the prince of demons that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drives out demons."

L.34: But the Pharisees were saying, "By the ruler of the demons {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} casts out the demons."

R.34: But the Pharisees said, "The ruler of demons gives {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the power to make demons leave."

decisions.choice: the ruler of the demons: Satan
decisions.reason: The Pharisees later name him Beelzebul (12:24), and Jesus answers the charge there (12:25-29).

decisions.choice: the verse is present, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is missing in a few manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts lack this verse. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.source: Καὶ περιῆγεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς πόλεις πάσας καὶ τὰς κώμας, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
records.gloss: And was going around the Jesus the towns all and the villages, teaching in the synagogues of them and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness.
pieces: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, announcing the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every illness.

L.35: And Jesus went around all the towns and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness.

R.35: Jesus traveled through all the towns and villages. He taught in their synagogues and told people the good news about God's kingdom. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed people of every kind of sickness and disease.

decisions.choice: the summary of 4:23 repeated
decisions.reason: The repeated summary closes the section that began at 4:23. Between them come Jesus's teaching (5-7) and his deeds (8-9).

decisions.choice: the same wording as 4:23 at each level
decisions.reason: The repeated summary is given in the same words, so readers can see the frame.

records.heading: The harvest is large

records.source: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἐσπλαγχνίσθη περὶ αὐτῶν ὅτι ἦσαν ἐσκυλμένοι καὶ ἐρριμμένοι ὡσεὶ πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα.
records.gloss: Having seen then the crowds he had compassion for them because they were troubled and thrown down as sheep not having a shepherd.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} felt deep pity for them, because they were worn out and abandoned, like sheep with no shepherd.

L.36: And seeing the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had compassion for them, because they were distressed and cast down, like sheep not having a shepherd.

R.36: When Jesus saw the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} felt sorry for them. They were tired and had no one to help them. They were like sheep without a shepherd to take care of them.

decisions.choice: had compassion: was moved deep within
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for the inner organs, thought of as the seat of feeling. It is used in the Gospels almost only of Jesus.

decisions.choice: sheep without a shepherd: Numbers 27:17; Ezekiel 34:5
decisions.reason: Moses prayed that Israel would not be like sheep without a shepherd. Ezekiel rebuked Israel's leaders for leaving the flock scattered and promised God himself would shepherd them (Ezekiel 34:11-16, 23).

decisions.choice: distressed and cast down: harassed, worn out and helpless
decisions.reason: The first word means troubled or mistreated; the second, thrown down or lying helpless.

records.source: τότε λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι·
records.gloss: Then he says to the disciples of him, The indeed harvest great, the but workers few;
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "The harvest is large, but there are few workers.

L.37: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "The harvest [is] plentiful, but the workers [are] few;

R.37: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "There is a big harvest of people to bring in, but there are only a few workers.

decisions.choice: the harvest: people ready to be gathered into God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Harvest can picture judgment (3:12; 13:39), but here it is the crowds ready to be gathered in.

decisions.choice: a big harvest of people to bring in
decisions.reason: Readable says what the harvest stands for.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense.

records.source: δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐκβάλῃ ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: ask therefore the Lord of the harvest that he may send out workers into the harvest of him.
pieces: So pray to the Lord of the harvest, and ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to send out workers into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest."

L.38: therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest."

R.38: So pray to God, who owns the harvest. Ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to send out more workers to bring in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest."

decisions.choice: the Lord of the harvest: God, who owns the field and the crop
decisions.reason: The harvest belongs to God, who sends the workers. In chapter 10 Jesus sends out the twelve.

decisions.choice: send out: drive out, send with urgency
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for casting out demons; it suggests a strong sending.

decisions.choice: God, who owns the harvest
decisions.reason: Readable names God.
